chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Bishr, from Ma'bad ibn Maysarah, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: When the sun passes the meridian in the length of the day, may a man pray al-zuhr and al-ʿasr? He said: “Yes, but I do not like that he should do that every day.”

key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun passed the meridian; the beginning of the zuhr prayer time
key_terms.طُولِ النَّهَارِ: the length or stretch of the day
key_terms.فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ: every day; indicating regular habitual practice

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray al-zuhr and al-'asr together every day after zawal?
ai.summary: This hadith states that it is permissible for a man to perform al-zuhr and al-'asr when the sun has declined past midday. However, Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام indicates that he does not prefer making this practice a daily habit, implying a distinction between permissibility and what is more preferable in regular practice.
